title: try out control scheme: select tab then pane e.g. cmd+2 > cmd+2 selects the 2nd tab > 2nd pane in that tab
creator: Alexander Terp

comments.body:
Built on main2 as d6620ea, behind `numbered_chords = "tab_then_pane"` in
~/.muster/config.toml. The default is unchanged, and saving the file switches
it live either way.

What to feel for while driving it:

- Pressing cmd+2 then cmd+3 expecting the third TAB, and landing on the third
  pane of tab 2. This is the prefix-key tax and it is not fixable inside the
  scheme. If it bites often, that is the answer.
- Whether acting on the first press feels right or premature: cmd+2 moves you
  before you have said what you wanted.
- Whether the numbers moving in the sidebar is enough to know which state you
  are in, or whether you end up guessing anyway. There is deliberately no
  timeout, so a first press waits forever - watch for coming back to the
  keyboard armed without knowing it.
- Whether nine tabs is a better nine than nine panes for the windows you
  actually run.

Left in in-progress: the card asks for a decision after using it, and that has
not happened yet.
comments.author: Alexander Terp
